title: Pricing Experiment Analysis Plan (2026 Q1) — Product Ops
content:
Owner: Chris Osei (Product Ops)
Reviewers/partners: Nikhil (PM Hosted API), Sana (stats/stop criteria), Rishi (FP&A), Emily (RevRec), Logan + Nadia (Telemetry), Mei (recon datasets), Jordan (GTM)
Doc purpose: Provide a single Q1 analysis plan for pricing/packaging experiments that (a) standardizes metrics + cohorts, (b) defines datasets + data quality checks needed to trust readouts, (c) sets a review cadence and stop/ship decisions with Finance + Eng.

0) Important caveat (meter changes overlap)
- We expect ongoing metering hardening changes during Q1 (tokens, retries, cache-hit attribution, embeddings batches, region dimension).
- All analyses MUST be segmented by “meter version regime” to avoid mixing pre/post fixes.
  - Minimum: pre-fix vs post-fix cutoff by deploy timestamp.
  - Preferred: use shadow-billing outputs (old_meter_* vs new_meter_*) where available to re-express historical usage in a consistent meter definition.
- Any metric based on billed tokens/requests must include a data-quality check section in the readout (freshness, drift vs ledger, duplicates rate, missing dimensions) + links to the sanity dashboard.

1) Experiment catalog + calendar (Q1 2026)
Source of truth: Confluence page “2026Q1 pricing experiments overview and guardrails”. This section is the analysis calendar view and what we need per experiment.

Experiment list (placeholder naming — see Confluence for final IDs/flags):
A. Variant B — Free tier & overage behavior update
- Hypothesis: clearer included usage + predictable overage reduces churn/charge disputes and increases conversion from free → paid.
- Primary levers: included monthly tokens, overage rate visibility, hard-limit vs soft-limit behavior, notification timing.

B. Variant C — “Starter bundle” vs pure usage-based
- Hypothesis: bundles improve new logo conversion and reduce cost anxiety without materially harming ARPU or margin.
- Primary levers: minimum monthly commit, included tokens, overage multiplier, rollover rules (if any).

C. Variant D — Dedicated add-on packaging for high-throughput customers
- Hypothesis: a clearer Dedicated add-on path increases expansion and improves gross margin predictability for heavy users.
- Primary levers: commit size, burst policy, SLA packaging, contract terms.

Calendar (analysis operations view)
- 2026-01-13 to 2026-01-24: instrumentation readiness + cohort tagging validation in staging (must be green before ramp)
- 2026-01-27: first limited ramp (<=10% eligible traffic for self-serve)
- 2026-02-03: expand ramp if data-quality SLOs green (freshness + drift checks)
- 2026-02-10: mid-point readout v1 (conversion + early retention signals + disputes)
- 2026-02-24: readout v2 (adds margin + longer retention window)
- 2026-03-10: final Q1 decision memo for exec staff review (or earlier stop)

Stop/go gates tied to data integrity (hard requirement)
- Do not proceed past 10% ramp if:
  - drift vs billing ledger > threshold for any top 20 accounts OR
  - duplicate usage event rate spikes above baseline OR
  - region/model dimension null rate exceeds threshold in experiment cohort.
(Thresholds tracked in PM-1842; until finalized, use “red/yellow/green” judgment with Logan/Nadia + Emily.)

2) Data sources needed (by question)
2.1 Experiment exposure / eligibility
- Experiment flags & cohort tagging events (from analytics/experimentation pipeline)
  - Required fields: account_id, project_id (if applicable), experiment_id, variant_id, exposure_ts, eligibility_reason (optional), channel (self-serve vs sales-led), plan_at_exposure.
  - Owner: Product analytics instrumentation via Eng (see PR-27533).

2.2 Usage + revenue (Hosted API)
- Usage events fact table (tokens/requests/latency dimensions)
  - Required fields (minimum): account_id, request_id, idempotency_key, ts_start/ts_end, model, region, endpoint (chat/completions/embeddings), raw_prompt_tokens, raw_completion_tokens, billed_prompt_tokens, billed_completion_tokens, billed_total_tokens, billed_requests, cache_hit (bool), cache_attribution (prefix/KV), retry_count, server_retry (bool), fallback_routed (bool), streaming (bool), tool_calls (count), status_code, error_class.
  - Notes: billed_* fields must be used for pricing; raw_* fields for behavioral/technical debugging.
  - Owners: Logan/Nadia.

- Billing ledger (invoice line item source)
  - Required fields: account_id, usage_date (billing timezone), meter_name, quantity, unit_price, amount, invoice_id, adjustment_id, credit_applied_id.
  - Owner: Emily/Finance; access restricted.

- Usage API exports (customer-facing reference)
  - Used to validate customer-visible numbers and dispute risk.
  - Needed fields: billed tokens vs raw tokens, cache-hit attribution (PR-27485), timezone behavior.

2.3 Costs + gross margin
- COGS allocation for Hosted API inference
  - Preferred: GPU-seconds or cost-per-token modeled by model+region+hardware class.
  - Inputs: runtime utilization dashboards, infra cost allocation tables, and model routing mix.
  - Owner: FP&A (Rishi) + Eng (Ethan/Caleb for infra data).

2.4 Qual + support burden (leading indicators)
- Support tickets tagged “billing/pricing dispute”, “usage export mismatch”, “double-charged retries”, “credits application”.
- Slack escalation count and time-to-resolution.
- Qual notes from Sales/SE calls (Fireflies) for top impacted accounts.

3) Metric definitions (standardized)
This section defines exactly what goes into readouts so we don’t debate definitions at every checkpoint.

3.1 Primary metrics
- Conversion (Free → Paid):
  - Definition: % of eligible new sign-ups that start a paid plan (or add payment method + cross the paid activation threshold) within N days of first API call.
  - Default windows: 7-day and 14-day.
  - Segment: self-serve only for primary read; sales-led tracked separately.

- Paid activation:
  - Definition: paid account reaches “meaningful usage” threshold (to be finalized; propose: >= X billed tokens OR >= Y billed requests) within 7 days of plan start.

- Retention:
  - D30 logo retention: paid accounts still active at day 30 (active defined by >= minimal billed usage).
  - D30 revenue retention: billed revenue day 0–30 vs prior window (for existing accounts).

- ARPU / Revenue per active account:
  - Definition: total billed amount (net of discounts, excluding one-time credits unless they are part of treatment) / # active paid accounts.
  - Report gross and net (net = after credits/discounts).

- Gross margin (modeled):
  - Definition: (Revenue – COGS) / Revenue over the same window.
  - Must be reported with the model-mix and cache-hit rate because these drive cost materially.

3.2 Guardrail metrics
- Billing dispute rate:
  - # accounts with billing-related support tickets / # billed accounts, weekly.

- Meter integrity guardrails (must be green for any readout used for decisions):
  - Freshness SLA: usage events and ledger exports available by T+X hours.
  - Drift vs ledger: aggregated billed quantity from usage events vs ledger quantity within threshold by day/account/meter.
  - Duplicate rate: % usage events with duplicate dedupe_key within dedupe window.
  - Null dimension rates: region/model/endpoint missing.

- Performance guardrails:
  - p95 latency and error rate by model/region for experiment vs control.

3.3 Notes on “billed tokens” vs “raw tokens”
- Use billed tokens for any pricing impact, ARPU, revenue, and customer fairness claims.
- Use raw tokens for behavioral analysis (prompt length distributions, completion length shifts) and debugging meter differences.
- Any time raw and billed diverge materially, annotate with the meter change log (e.g., caching attribution, retry dedupe, tool-call accounting).

4) Cohorts + segmentation strategy
Goal: prevent confounding; make sure results are interpretable.

4.1 Core splits (always shown)
- Acquisition channel: self-serve vs sales-led
- Customer lifecycle: new (first_seen within 30 days) vs existing
- Geo/region: NA/EU/APAC (and specific cloud region where needed)
- Model family: top 5 models by usage + “other”
- Endpoint type: chat/completions vs embeddings
- Cache behavior: high cache-hit vs low cache-hit (define by account-level cache_hit_rate quartiles)

4.2 Exclusions / confounders (default)
- Accounts under active invoice dispute at start of experiment (to avoid behavioral changes driven by finance escalation)
- Accounts impacted by known meter incidents (list maintained weekly with Logan/Nadia)
- Accounts with contract-only bespoke pricing unless explicitly included as “sales-led cohort”

4.3 Power / sample considerations (Sana)
- For conversion experiments: minimum detectable effect assumptions and minimum sample sizes must be documented per variant.
- For margin: variance is high due to model mix; require at least 2–4 weeks of steady-state traffic (unless effect is very large).

5) Analysis approach (what we will actually compute)
5.1 For conversion experiments (new self-serve)
- Unit of analysis: account (not request)
- Intent-to-treat: based on exposure to variant
- Primary method: difference in proportions (with confidence intervals), plus logistic regression controlling for initial model used, region, day-of-week.
- Secondary: survival curves (time to paid) for variants.

5.2 For revenue/margin on existing customers
- Unit of analysis: account-week
- Method: difference-in-differences where possible (pre/post within account, comparing to control), controlling for seasonality.
- Required: stable meter regime segmentation.

5.3 Dispute/support impact
- Track ticket creation rate and severity; annotate major incidents.
- Qualitative coding for top 20 tickets (themes: token counting, retries, cache, exports timezone, credits).

6) Readout template (standard)
Every checkpoint readout should include:
1) Experiment status: ramp %, dates, eligibility notes
2) Data quality status (freshness, drift, duplicates, nulls) + links
3) Primary metric table (conversion/retention/ARPU/margin) with CI where applicable
4) Segment breakdown (at least the core splits)
5) Guardrails (support tickets, disputes, latency/errors)
6) Interpretation + decision recommendation (continue/ramp/stop/ship)
7) Open questions + next steps + owners

7) Review cadence + operating rhythm
Weekly (Tues): Data quality + meter status sync (Product Ops + Telemetry + RevRec)
- Attendees: Chris, Logan, Nadia, Emily, Mei, Sana (as needed)
- Output: “green/yellow/red” for using data in decision-making; incident annotations.

Biweekly (Thurs): Experiment performance readout (Product + FP&A + RevOps)
- Attendees: Nikhil, Chris, Rishi, Jordan, Sana
- Output: decision log entry + next ramp/stop recommendation.

Monthly: Exec update (CPO/CFO/CRO + Eng sponsor)
- Summarize results, recommended packaging guidance updates, and any billing-risk actions.

8) Decision log + documentation
- Decisions must be recorded with:
  - experiment_id + variant
  - date
  - metrics snapshot
  - meter regime statement (“uses billed_token_vX with shadow compare”)
  - sign-offs: Product (Nikhil), FP&A (Rishi), RevRec (Emily) for revenue-impacting changes.

9) Action items (as of 2026-02-22)
- [Chris] Align exact conversion and activation definitions with RevOps instrumentation (due 2026-02-26)
- [Sana] Publish stop criteria defaults + minimum sample size table per experiment (due 2026-02-28)
- [Logan/Nadia] Provide meter version change log timestamps for Q1 (for pre/post segmentation) (due 2026-02-25)
- [Mei] Confirm Finance-readable export table schema for recon + experiment joins (due 2026-03-01)
- [Rishi] Confirm COGS allocation approach for margin readouts (model+region level) (due 2026-03-05)

Appendix A: Field mapping (quick)
- exposure join key: account_id + exposure_ts <= usage_ts
- usage aggregation grain for readouts: account-day and account-week
- revenue grain: account-day (ledger) rolled to account-week
- timezone: use billing timezone for ledger alignment; explicitly call out if usage export is UTC-based.

Appendix B: Known risks
- Meter changes can flip measured effects (especially if prior logic double-counted retries or missed cache-hit attribution).
- Model routing changes (fallbacks, region failover) can change cost and perceived value; must be tracked as a parallel timeseries.
- Sales-led exceptions (discounts/credits) can swamp treatment effects; keep separate unless experiment explicitly targets sales-led packaging.

Notes to self:
- Make sure readout v2 includes a “customer fairness narrative” slide: billed vs raw tokens explanation, retries policy, caching policy. This keeps Sales from improvising.
- If we see conversion improvements but dispute rate increases, push for messaging/UX + usage dashboard changes before pricing is rolled out globally.
